new_statements.quote: Remarque 2. A la question, soulevée par Jacqueline THOMAS, de savoir si les différences de traitement tonal en fonction du type syllabique ne pourraient s'expliquer par la présence d'un accent dans les langues concernées, on doit répondre négativement : aucune ne présente actuellement de phénomène d'accent, d'intensité ni de longueur. L'hypothèse sera reposée en diachronie, lors de l'interprétation des correspondances phoniques (p. 345). [p. 345:] L'absence d'accent dans les langues actuelles n'impose pas cette solution en proto-gbaya, mais l'hypothèse est envisageable à un niveau antérieur de l'évolution.
new_statements.translation: Remark 2. To the question, raised by Jacqueline Thomas, of whether the differences in tonal treatment according to syllable type could be explained by the presence of an accent in the languages concerned, the answer must be negative: none of them currently shows any phenomenon of accent, of intensity or of length. The hypothesis will be raised again in diachrony, in interpreting the sound correspondences (p. 345). [p. 345:] The absence of accent in the present-day languages does not force this solution for proto-Gbaya, but the hypothesis can be entertained for an earlier stage of the evolution.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Manza is a tone language (Moñino's Gbaya-Manza-Ngbaka languages have level tones H/M/L plus contours and a morphological tone rule 'MR', which p. 285 says applies in Manza); no word-level accent, intensity or length phenomenon exists in any of the 21 languages surveyed, Manza included. No stress-placement rule is given because there is none to give.
new_statements.exceptions: None. The only qualification is diachronic: an accent is entertained for a stage earlier than proto-Gbaya, not for any modern language.
new_statements.domain_note: Blanket statement over the 21 languages of the monograph, not a Manza-specific paragraph; Manza is named on the same page (MR discussion) and its data (c. 1200 words and sentences) are Bouquiaux's unpublished files (p. 51), not Moñino's own fieldwork. Word-level phonology (tonal treatment by syllable type: CV, CVC, CVCV, CVCVCV); no citation-form vs. phrase distinction drawn. The language-specific Manza chapter of the same book was not reachable and would supersede this.
new_statements.identity_note: Manza [mzv] manz1243 (Mandja/Manja), CAR. The Moñino 1995 statement covers the whole Gbaya-Manza-Ngbaka set of 21 languages; its Manza data are Bouquiaux's unpublished files (dialect not stated on the pages seen). Distinct from Ngbaka Manza [ngg] ngba1287 (also in the same book, and described by Sélézilo 2008 held in ngba1287/), and from Eboué 1918's 'Mandjia de la région de Damara près Bangui' which is the same language [mzv] per hh.bib.

new_statements.relation_note: This is the passage already recorded in existing_statements (Moñino 1995 p. 285 / p. 345); The catalog record for Manza has an empty rule field; this source supports filling it with 'no word stress (tonal language)'. The Manza chapter pages are not yet obtained held by the project and Google Books (books.google.com.uk and the volumes API) is could not be reached by automated download, but the in-volume search shows no further accent statement exists there.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Manza, like all 21 Gbaya-Manza-Ngbaka languages of the book, is a tone language with no accent, intensity or length phenomenon; word stress is absent. Manza is named on the same page (area b of the tonal-replacement table: the MR amalgamates with the first term in ali, ngbaka-manza, manza, ngbaka). Moñino's Manza data are c. 1200 words and sentences from Bouquiaux's unpublished files (p. 51), not his own fieldwork.
new_statements.exceptions: Scope nuance: Remarque 2 answers a question about 'les langues concernées' (the area-a languages whose tonal treatment depends on syllable type; Manza is in area b), but 'aucune ne présente actuellement..' and the p. 345 'absence d'accent dans les langues actuelles' are stated for the present-day languages generally. The Google Books in-volume search for 'accent' (held) gives only 4 hits in the whole book, pp. 60, 285, 345, 705, so the Manza chapter itself contains no separate accent statement.
new_statements.identity_note: Probst 2018 (survey of Feb-Mar 1994) distinguishes Manza [mzv] from Ngbaka Manza [ngg] and describes two Manza dialect zones: west (Bouca; R.N. 4 Marali-Bolom; called [yakõ]) and east (Kaga Bandoro-Dékoa, Grivaï, Mala; called [ya]), with intra-zone differences said to be tonal. Moñino 1995 treats 'manza' and 'ngbaka-manza' as separate languages among his 21; his Manza data are c. 1200 words and sentences from Bouquiaux's unpublished files (p. 51), dialect not specified on the pages.

tone_statements.citation: Moore, Troy Christopher (révision par Paul Murrell; traduit par Nathalie Saint-André). 2016 [2000]. Proposition d'orthographe de la langue mandja (révisé). Bangui: ACATBA (Association Centrafricaine pour la Traduction de la Bible et l'Alphabétisation) et SIL RCA / SIL International. iv+42 pp. ('Mars 2000, révisé juillet 2016 après l'atelier de tonalité janvier 2015'; PDF metadata title 'Manza Phonology Analysis', created 2017-10-12; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).
tone_statements.quote: [p. 4, §2.1] Selon le document « Manza Phonological Statement » (Moore 2000), la langue mandja possède trois tons, 29 consonnes et 7 voyelles (parmi elles, 5 ont des équivalences nasales). [...] [p. 6, §3.1] Dans la langue mandja, le ton lexical est particulièrement présent (plus de 15% des noms contenus dans le lexique se différencient par leur tonalité) ; le ton grammatical est lui-aussi fondamental : il indique à quel temps sont conjugués les verbes. [...] - le ton haut sera marqué par un accent circonflexe sur la voyelle - le ton moyen avec un tréma - le ton bas n'a pas de signe particulier.
tone_statements.translation: [p. 4] According to the 'Manza Phonological Statement' (Moore 2000), the Mandja language has three tones, 29 consonants and 7 vowels (5 of which have nasal counterparts). [...] [p. 6] In Mandja, lexical tone is particularly prominent (more than 15% of the nouns in the lexicon are distinguished by their tone); grammatical tone is also fundamental: it indicates the tense in which verbs are conjugated. [...] - high tone will be marked with a circumflex on the vowel - mid tone with a diaeresis - low tone has no special sign.
tone_statements.locator: p. 4, §2.1 'Analyse phonologique' with Tableau 1; p. 6, §3.1 'La tonalité'; verb tone §3.1.2 pp. 7-9; tonème relationnel §4.3 p. 18-19

sources.quote: Manza does not appear to have any phonemic stress, and is therefore similar to other Gbaya languages in this respect. However, stress over certain lexemes is quite noticeable, such as over ideophones, but this has not yet been studied at length.
